title: Bread Pakoda

ingredients.title: For the Filling
items: Fresh coriander leaves – 2 tbsp, finely chopped

ingredients.title: For the Batter
items: Water – as needed to make a smooth, thick batter

ingredients.title: For Assembly & Frying
items: Neutral oil – as needed for deep frying

instruction.title: Prepare the Filling
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; let them splutter.
Add chopped green chili and grated ginger; sauté for about 1 minute.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt; mix well.
Add mashed potatoes, garam masala, and chaat masala.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring well to blend the spices.
Add chopped coriander leaves, mix, and remove from heat.
Let the potato filling cool completely.

instruction.title: Prepare the Batter
steps: Add gram flour, turmeric powder, red chili powder, asafoetida, and salt to a mixing bowl.
Gradually add water while whisking to form a smooth, thick batter.
Adjust the consistency so it is similar to pancake batter but slightly thicker.

instruction.title: Assemble the Pakodas
steps: Take a bread slice and cut off the edges if desired.
Spread a generous layer of cooled potato filling over the slice.
Cover with another bread slice to form a sandwich.
Press lightly to secure the sandwich and seal the edges.
Repeat with the remaining bread slices and filling.

instruction.title: Frying
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Dip each stuffed bread sandwich into the gram flour batter, coating it evenly.
Carefully place the coated sandwich into the hot oil.
Fry over medium heat until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Cut each fried sandwich into halves or desired portions.
Serve hot with green chutney, tamarind chutney, or ketchup.

chefTips: Filling: Cool the potato filling completely before assembling to prevent the bread from becoming soggy.
Batter texture: Keep the besan batter thick enough to coat the bread evenly without sliding off.
Frying temperature: Maintain medium heat so the coating becomes crisp and golden without burning.
Bread: Regular white bread works well; slightly thick slices are easier to handle and hold more filling.
Serving: Bread pakodas are best served immediately while hot and crisp.
